207: def smooth_segments(mapped, grid):

210:     half = points // 2
211:     kernel = np.r_[0.5, np.ones(points - 2), 0.5] / (points - 1)
212:     raw = np.full(grid.size, np.nan)
213:     smooth = np.full(grid.size, np.nan)
214:     for segment in np.unique(mapped["segment"]):
215:         use = mapped["segment"] == segment
216:         order = np.argsort(mapped["arrival"][use])
217:         times, unique = np.unique(mapped["arrival"][use][order], return_index=True)
218:         values = mapped["flux"][use][order][unique]
219:         inside = np.flatnonzero((grid >= times[0]) & (grid <= times[-1]))
220:         if not len(inside):
221:             continue
222:         raw[inside] = np.interp(grid[inside], times, values)
223:         if len(inside) >= points:
224:             smooth[inside[half:-half]] = np.convolve(raw[inside], kernel, mode="valid")

## 1. 3D Ideal MHD Equations in Spherical Coordinates $(r, \theta, \phi)$

### 1.1 Conservative Formulation & Frame Choice
Let $(r, \theta, \phi)$ denote radius $r \in [r_{\rm in}, r_{\rm out}]$ ($r_{\rm in} = 0.1\text{ AU} = 21.5\,R_\odot$, $r_{\rm out} \ge 2.2\text{ AU}$), colatitude $\theta \in [\theta_{\min}, \pi-\theta_{\min}]$ (e.g., $\theta \in [30^\circ, 150^\circ]$ covering $\pm 60^\circ$ latitude, avoiding the polar coordinate singularity), and azimuth $\phi \in [0, 2\pi)$.

In Gaussian/Heaviside-Lorentz (code) units where magnetic permeability $\mu_0 = 1$ (absorbable via $\mathbf{B}_{\rm code} = \mathbf{B}/\sqrt{4\pi}$ CGS or $\mathbf{B}/\sqrt{\mu_0}$ SI), the conservative state vector is
$$\mathbf{U} = \begin{pmatrix} \rho \\ \rho v_r \\ \rho v_\theta \\ \rho v_\phi \\ B_r \\ B_\theta \\ B_\phi \\ E \end{pmatrix}, \qquad E = \frac{p}{\gamma - 1} + \frac{1}{2}\rho v^2 + \frac{1}{2}B^2, \qquad p^* = p + \frac{1}{2}B^2.$$

On a spherical finite-volume mesh with cell volume $\Delta V = \frac{1}{3}(r_{i+1/2}^3 - r_{i-1/2}^3)(\cos\theta_{j-1/2} - \cos\theta_{j+1/2})\Delta\phi$, the governing conservation law in an **inertial heliocentric frame** (e.g. HEEQ / Ecliptic J2000) is:
$$\frac{\partial \mathbf{U}}{\partial t} + \frac{1}{r^2}\frac{\partial}{\partial r}\!\left(r^2 \mathbf{F}_r\right) + \frac{1}{r\sin\theta}\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta}\!\left(\sin\theta\,\mathbf{F}_\theta\right) + \frac{1}{r\sin\theta}\frac{\partial \mathbf{F}_\phi}{\partial \phi} = \mathbf{S}_{\rm geom} + \mathbf{S}_{\rm grav} + \mathbf{S}_{\rm divB}.$$

The directional flux vectors $\mathbf{F}_d$ ($d \in \{r, \theta, \phi\}$) are:
$$\mathbf{F}_r = \begin{pmatrix} \rho v_r \\ \rho v_r^2 + p^* - B_r^2 \\ \rho v_r v_\theta - B_r B_\theta \\ \rho v_r v_\phi - B_r B_\phi \\ 0 \\ v_r B_\theta - v_\theta B_r \\ v_r B_\phi - v_\phi B_r \\ (E + p^*)v_r - B_r(\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{B}) \end{pmatrix}, \quad
\mathbf{F}_\theta = \begin{pmatrix} \rho v_\theta \\ \rho v_\theta v_r - B_\theta B_r \\ \rho v_\theta^2 + p^* - B_\theta^2 \\ \rho v_\theta v_\phi - B_\theta B_\phi \\ v_\theta B_r - v_r B_\theta \\ 0 \\ v_\theta B_\phi - v_\phi B_\theta \\ (E + p^*)v_\theta - B_\theta(\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{B}) \end{pmatrix}, \quad
\mathbf{F}_\phi = \begin{pmatrix} \rho v_\phi \\ \rho v_\phi v_r - B_\phi B_r \\ \rho v_\phi v_\theta - B_\phi B_\theta \\ \rho v_\phi^2 + p^* - B_\phi^2 \\ v_\phi B_r - v_r B_\phi \\ v_\phi B_\theta - v_\theta B_\phi \\ 0 \\ (E + p^*)v_\phi - B_\phi(\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{B}) \end{pmatrix}.$$

### 1.2 Geometric, Gravitational, and Corotating-Frame Source Terms
- **Spherical Geometric Source Terms ($\mathbf{S}_{\rm geom}$):**
  $$\mathbf{S}_{\rm geom} = \begin{pmatrix}
  0 \\[3pt]
  \dfrac{2p^*}{r} + \dfrac{\rho(v_\theta^2 + v_\phi^2) - (B_\theta^2 + B_\phi^2)}{r} \\[6pt]
  \dfrac{p^*\cot\theta}{r} + \dfrac{\rho(v_\phi^2\cot\theta - v_r v_\theta) - (B_\phi^2\cot\theta - B_r B_\theta)}{r} \\[6pt]
  -\dfrac{\rho v_\phi(v_r + v_\theta\cot\theta) - B_\phi(B_r + B_\theta\cot\theta)}{r} \\[6pt]
  0 \\[3pt]
  \dfrac{v_\theta B_r - v_r B_\theta}{r} \\[6pt]
  \dfrac{v_\phi B_r - v_r B_\phi + (v_\phi B_\theta - v_\theta B_\phi)\cot\theta}{r} \\[6pt]
  0
  \end{pmatrix}.$$
  *(Note: To preserve uniform pressure equilibria $\nabla p = 0$ to machine precision on coarse grids, discretize the pressure terms $\frac{2p^*}{r}$ and $\frac{p^*\cot\theta}{r}$ using the finite-volume cell-face area identity or the non-conservative $\partial_r p^*$ / $\frac{1}{r}\partial_\theta p^*$ cell-centered reconstruction).*
- **Solar Gravity Source Terms ($\mathbf{S}_{\rm grav}$):**
  $$\mathbf{S}_{\rm grav} = \left(0,\; -\rho \frac{G M_\odot}{r^2},\; 0,\; 0,\; 0,\; 0,\; 0,\; -\rho v_r \frac{G M_\odot}{r^2}\right)^T, \qquad GM_\odot = 1.3271244\times 10^{20}\text{ m}^3\text{ s}^{-2}.$$

     $$\frac{\partial \psi}{\partial t} + c_h^2 (\nabla\cdot\mathbf{B}) = -\frac{c_h^2}{c_p^2}\psi,$$

## 3. Passive Scalar Advection for Heavy-Ion Abundance / Charge-State Ratio ($n_{\rm hi}/n_p$)

### 3.1 Physical Justification & Conservation Equation
Solar wind heavy-ion charge states ($\text{O}^{6+,7+,8+}$, $\text{C}^{5+,6+}$, $\text{N}^{6+,7+}$, $\text{Ne}^{8+,9+}$, $\text{Mg}$, $\text{Si}$, $\text{Fe}$) freeze in within the low corona ($r \approx 1.5\text{--}4\,R_\odot$) where the electron density drops below the recombination/ionization timescale threshold. Beyond $r_{\rm in} = 21.5\,R_\odot$, ionization and recombination timescales exceed $10^7\text{ s}$ (months), whereas the solar wind transit time to $2\text{ AU}$ is $\sim 5\text{--}10\text{ days}$ ($\lesssim 10^6\text{ s}$). Moreover, all solar wind ions share the same bulk MHD flow velocity $\mathbf{v}$ (differential streaming is $\lesssim$ a few percent of $v_A$, negligible at $r > 0.3\text{ AU}$).

Therefore, any heavy-ion number ratio $f_s \equiv n_s / n_p$ (either a single composite SWCX-active heavy-ion fraction $f_{\rm hi} = n_{\rm hi}/n_p$ or multiple species scalars $f_{\text{O}^{7+}}, f_{\text{O}^{8+}}, f_{\text{C}^{6+}}, f_{\text{N}^{7+}}$) satisfies the **material derivative advection equation**:
$$\frac{\partial f_s}{\partial t} + (\mathbf{v}\cdot\nabla) f_s = 0 \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \frac{\partial (\rho f_s)}{\partial t} + \nabla\cdot(\rho f_s \mathbf{v}) = 0.$$

### 3.2 Finite-Volume Discretization
In the finite-volume solver, evolve the conserved tracer density $C_s = \rho f_s$ using the **exact mass flux** $F_{\rho, d}$ already computed by the HLL/HLLD Riemann solver at each cell interface:
$$F_{C_s, i+1/2} = F_{\rho, i+1/2} \cdot \begin{cases} f_{s, L}^{i+1/2} & \text{if } F_{\rho, i+1/2} \ge 0, \\[4pt] f_{s, R}^{i+1/2} & \text{if } F_{\rho, i+1/2} < 0, \end{cases}$$
where $f_{s, L/R}^{i+1/2}$ are TVD/PLM (e.g. minmod or MC) reconstructed interface values of $f_s = C_s / \rho$.
- **Strict Consistency & Maximum Principle:** Because $F_{\rho, i+1/2} > 0$ everywhere in the supersonic radial flow and the upwind reconstruction of $f_s$ is TVD, $f_s^{\rm new} = C_s^{\rm new}/\rho^{\rm new}$ is **guaranteed** to remain strictly bounded within $[f_{s,\min}, f_{s,\max}]$ with zero conservation error even across strong CIR forward/reverse shocks.
